newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Bratislava, Belgrade aim to boost bilateral trade.
newsitem.headline: Bratislava, Belgrade aim to boost bilateral trade.

text.p: Slovakia said on Thursday that it wanted to get the annual level of bilateral trade with Yugoslavia back to $400 million now that U.N. sanctions have been lifted against Yugoslavia.

"The lifting of United Nations sanctions against Yugoslavia has created conditions for a revival of relations between our countries," Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar told a news conference after meeting Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic.
"This year we would like our mutual trade to reach a turnover of $400 million which it was before sanctions were imposed," Meciar said.
"I think this figure is realistic, but at present things are moving slower than we expected," Kontic said. "But we are seeking ways to solve this."
Kontic, on a three-day visit to Slovakia, and Meciar discussed setting up a free trade zone and a possible agreement to prevent double taxation.
Meciar said Slovakia supported the efforts of Yugoslavia, which comprises Serbia and Montenegro, to become reintegrated in all international political, social and economic structures.
